newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK air cargo import customs system awaits funding.
newsitem.headline: HK air cargo import customs system awaits funding.

text.p: Hong Kong's Customs and Excise Department is awaiting Government funding approval to install an import cargo clearance computer system at the new Chek Lap Kok airport, the department's assistant commissioner David Tong told Reuters.
Tong, in charge of the airport, control points and drugs investigation, said in an interview that a feasibility study has alreadybeen carried out.
" We have government support and are awaiting the funding go ahead which I am confident of getting soon," he added probably within the next few weeks.
Tong said the computer would link his department with the new airport's two air cargo terminal operators, airlines, freight forwarders and major warehouses for import cargo clearance.
Talks have already been held with airlines, express cargo companies, freight forwarders and industry spokesman who support his department's initiative, he said.

"If we can tell importers what the customs requirements are through the computer it will be much more efficient. We should have better data which would mean more accurate selection (for Customs checks) and help the whole process of cargo clearance," Tong said in an interview. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
